full_judgment:
20. In this case, the Court, by the conduct of the parties, has proceeded on a presumption that the parties have agreed to arbitrate on the dispute under the provisions of the Arbitration Act, 2001 inasmuch as when respondent No. 6 approached the Court upon invoking section 12 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 and the present petitioner-DNCC initially submitted the name of Mr Shamsuddin Chowdhury, as an arbitrator from its side before the District Judge Court of Dhaka and, thereafter, replaced him by Mr AKM Faiz, any one with ordinary prudence shall be of the view that the parties have mutually consented to take recourse to the provisions of the Arbitration Act, 2001 and, with regard to the issue of the legal requirements of issuance of notice to other party, in absence of any objection from the petitioner-DNCC's side, it was very usual for the Court to think that either the said legal requirement has been complied with by the initiating party or it has been waived by the other party. Therefore, this Court does not find any substance in the petitioner-DNCC's aforesaid pleas. 

 23. Usually the initiating party of the arbitration approaches the High Court Division/ the District Judge Court proposing name of an arbitrator. However, the High Court Division/the District Judge Court is not bound, be it for formation of a single-member tribunal or a three-member tribunal, to include the said proposed person in formation of the tribunal inasmuch as when the parties mutually form the tribunal, the law prescribes that the appointments of arbitrator/s are to be made as per the choices of the parties to arbitration but whenever there will be a disagreement among the arbitrators as to appointment of the Chairman, it is the High Court Division/the District Judge Court which has exclusively been empowered to appoint the Chairman, either upon taking or without taking name/s from the parties to the arbitration. However, eventually if both the parties come to an agreement as to appointment of the Chairman during pendency of the section 12 application, then, the case being redundant should be non-prosecuted. Similarly, in the case of appointment of a single arbitrator for formation of a one-member tribunal if the initiating party comes up with name of an arbitrator and the other party does not appear before the High Court Division/the District Judge Court, it shall appoint the arbitrator of its own choice by ignoring the name supplied by the initiating party, so that the other party does not consider the tribunal to be partisan. The same principle shall also be applied for formation of a three-member tribunal by the High Court Division/the District Judge Court in a scenario when the other party does not supply the name of an arbitrator from its side upon receipt of notice containing the name of the arbitrator from the initiating party. The rationale behind non-inclusion of the name supplied by the initiating party in the one/three-member tribunal to be formed by the High Court Division/the District Judge Court is to provide security/protection to the other party through elimination of the possibility of bias, for it is of fundamental importance that justice must not only be done, but also be seen to be done; that is to say, if the High Court Division/the District Judge Court forms the one/three-member tribunal in the absence of the other party, the other party should not feel itself sided/cornered when it will appear before the tribunal. The scheme of the law regarding formation of an arbitration tribunal is such that when the parties to the arbitration form a three-member arbitration tribunal upon appointing two arbitrators from each sides without the Court's aid, none of the arbitrators shall he considered biased merely because of being appointed by the parties to the arbitration, but since the scenario becomes different because of non-appointment of an arbitrator from the other side despite receiving the notice issued by the initiating party, the said presumption, in the absence of the other party, does not become applicable in the case of formation of the tribunal by the High Court Division/the District Judge Court, be it for constitution of a one-member tribunal or a three-member tribunal.
